notes:
Summary: Meridian builds an IDE copilot (VS Code native extension) for enterprise dev teams. Primary acceptance criteria revolve around snappy interactive completions: TTFT target 35-60ms for single-line completions, tail latency <150ms, jitter (variance) under 10–15ms so suggestions don’t appear to 'stutter'. They are cost-sensitive and want token-budget tuning defaults (slot-based budgets per user/session) to keep RU under $0.002 per completion on average.

POC findings so far (raw):
- Integration: Swift + TypeScript client in extension, streaming endpoint works end-to-end.
- Observed TTFT: hosted dev pool median 120ms, 95th 260ms. Users report perceived lag >120ms = aborted completions.
- Jitter: intermittent spikes correlated with batching windows on multi-tenant backend.
- Backpressure: Editor experiences small hiccups when model emits bursts — need graceful backpressure (smaller chunks, client-side token budget to stop/resume).
- Model pinning: Meridian wants ability to pin to a quantized low-latency variant (redwood-q4b) for IDE paths and fall back to higher-quality float model for code explainers.

Quotes / call snippets: "If the first token takes more than 100ms, devs notice and hit escape" — product lead."We'd rather drop tokens than let the editor block for long tail latency" — lead frontend eng.

Technical asks / acceptance criteria (explicit):
- TTFT median <= 60ms for short completions (<=60 tokens) in dedicated pool at scale (100 concurrent users).
- 95th percentile latency < 150ms.
- Jitter (stddev of TTFT) < 15ms across sample window.
- Streaming granularity: support 8–16 token mini-chunks and immediate flush on first token.
- Token-budget controls per user/session with server-side enforcement and soft-client-side hints for graceful truncation.
- Model-version pinning + routing policy for canary/rollback without extension update.

Operational notes:
- Wants per-route dashboards (token cost, TTFT histograms).
- Prefers dedicated GPU pool with burst to hosted during peak.
- Security: SSO + audit logging required; EU code teams require residency.

POC actions owned:
- SE (Ethan): create TTFT harness that runs 100 concurrent simulated editors; collect per-token timings and jitter curve (due 2026-03-18).
- AE (Sofia): negotiate short trial credit and draft procurement SOW for dedicated pool.
- Infra (Meridian): add client-side backpressure handler to drop/truncate suggestions when server signals budget-exceeded.

Next steps: schedule dedicated-pool run (A100 vs T4 comparison), finalize model-pin RFC, produce cost tradeoffs for token-budget defaults.
